page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.medium is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 AWS Graviton3 processor. Configured with a single dedicated physical core running at 2.6 GHz, the instance delivers 1 vCPU alongside 2.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The processor is backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded computational efficiency alongside typical single-core entry-level constraints. Single-core performance tests such as stress-ng (1515.58) and Geekbench (1430.0) place within the average category. However, because the instance features only one dedicated core, aggregate multi-core throughput scores are identical to single-core values, resulting in lower relative rankings compared to multi-core configurations. Memory bandwidth registers at 97.18 GB/sec for small cached reads and 30.49 GB/sec for large uncached reads, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 9.19 GB/sec.

A key differentiator of the c7gd series is the inclusion of direct-attached high-speed storage. The c7gd.medium comes bundled with a 59 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral I/O without incurring external volume network transport latency. Networking is baseline rated at 1 Gbps. The primary architectural tradeoff is the small memory footprint and single-core limit, which restricts parallel batch operations and memory-heavy caching. Qualitatively, it delivers an economical entry point for lightweight ARM-native microservices, local caching layers, edge data pre-processing, and CI/CD testing environments needing fast ephemeral storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 Graviton3 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. It is equipped with 1 vCPU, 2.0 GB of memory, and 59 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage on the Nitro hypervisor. Single-core compute benchmarks such as Geekbench (1430.0) and stress-ng (1515.58) demonstrate solid single-thread execution efficiency, while multi-core metrics naturally reflect the single-core hardware ceiling. With baseline 1 Gbps networking and dedicated hardware crypto extensions, the instance avoids CPU oversubscription. However, total memory capacity remains constrained at 2.0 GB, limiting large memory arrays or high-concurrency tasks. The c7gd.medium is well matched for lightweight ARM64 development, small-scale web endpoints, ephemeral data pre-processing, and microservices requiring fast local disk I/O.
